syllabusTopics: Limits and continuity: limits of a function, indeterminate forms, algebraic properties of limits (without proof), basic theorems on limits of algebraic, trigonometric, exponential and logarithmic functions
Continuity of a function, types of discontinuity, graphs of discontinuous function
Derivatives: derivative of a function, derivatives of algebraic, trigonometric, inverse trigonometric, exponential and logarithmic functions by definition (simple forms)
Rules of differentiation; derivatives of parametric and implicit functions; higher order derivatives
Geometric interpretation of derivative; monotonicity of a function, interval of monotonicity, extreme values of a function, concavity, points of inflection
Anti-derivatives: integration using basic integrals, integration by substitution and by parts methods
The definite integral; the definite integral as an area under the given curve; area between two curves

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The **differentiation toolkit** turns the table into universal machinery. **Product rule** (fg)′ = f′g + fg′ (sin x·cos x → cos²x − sin²x = cos 2x, NEB 2023) and **quotient rule** (f′g − fg′)/g² are the workhorses; the **chain rule** dy/dx = dy/du·du/dx is the master — outer table, inner derivative, multiply.…

rows.text: - (fg)′ = f′g + fg′; (f/g)′ = (f′g − fg′)/g² - chain: dy/dx = (dy/du)(du/dx) - parametric: dy/dx = (dy/dt)/(dx/dt); d²y/dx² = (d/dt(dy/dx))/(dx/dt) - log-diff: y = u^v ⟹ y′ = y(v′ ln u + vu′/u)

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***The x^x litmus test*** - neither power nor exponential rule applies when both base and exponent vary: ln y = x ln x is the universal escape hatch.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The Differentiation Toolkit **Rules of differentiation** — product, quotient, chain — plus **parametric, implicit and higher-order derivatives**: the machinery that makes every function differentiable in practice.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 Product and quotient rules - **Product:** (fg)′ = f′g + fg′ (proved by adding and subtracting f(x+h)g(x)). **Quotient:** (f/g)′ = (f′g − fg′)/g² (g ≠ 0). - **Memory:** product keeps order symmetry; quotient is "low d-high minus high d-low over low squared".…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: u^v both variable: ln y first. Parametric: dy/dt over dx/dt; second derivative divides by dx/dt again. Implicit: differentiate through, solve linearly for y'.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **NEB 2023 (verified PYQ): Find the derivative of y = sin x · cos x using the product rule. (3m)** — **Product rule:** y′ = (sin x)′·cos x + sin x·(cos x)′ = **cos x·cos x + sin x·(−sin x)** = cos²x − sin²x. **Simplify:** by the double-angle identity, cos²x − sin²x = **cos 2x**.…  ·  **NEB 2022 (verified PYQ): Differentiate with respect to x: (i) y = xˣ, (ii) y = sin²x · eˣ, (iii) y = (1+x)^{1/x}. (3m)** — **(i) Logarithmic differentiation** (both base and exponent variable — neither single rule applies): ln y = x ln x ⟹ y′/y = 1·ln x + x·(1/x) = ln x + 1 ⟹ **y′ = xˣ(ln x + 1)**.…

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: For "show that" derivative questions, keep y in the final answer when the target form does - substituting it out loses the match.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: The chain rule is the master rule: outer table derivative times inner derivative - product, quotient and every composite reduce to it.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Product rule: (fg)' = f'g + fg'. Quotient rule: (f/g)' = (f'g - fg')/g^2. Chain rule: (f o g)' = f'(g(x)) g'(x), i.e. dy/dx = dy/du du/dx - the master rule. Parametric: x = x(t), y = y(t) => dy/dx = (dy/dt)/(dx/dt); d^2y/dx^2 = [d/dt(dy/dx)]/(dx/dt) - divide by dx/dt again.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Gear trains multiply rates like the chain rule: output speed = gear ratio (outer) times input speed (inner) - differentiation's mechanics is mechanics.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: **NEB 2023 (verified PYQ): If y = (sin x)^{cos x}, show that dy/dx = y(cos x · cot x − sin x · log_e(sin x)). (3m)** — **Step 1 — take logs** (u^v with both parts variable): ln y = cos x · ln(sin x).…  ·  **NEB-style (6m): For the cycloid x = a(θ − sin θ), y = a(1 − cos θ), find dy/dx and d²y/dx².** — **First derivative (parametric rule):** dx/dθ = a(1 − cos θ); dy/dθ = a sin θ ⟹ dy/dx = a sin θ/[a(1 − cos θ)] = sin θ/(1 − cos θ).…  ·  **NEB-style (5m): If x² + xy + y² = 7, find dy/dx by implicit differentiation and the equation of the tangent at (1, 2).** — **Differentiate through in x** (y is y(x); the product term needs the product rule): 2x + [y + x·y′] + 2y·y′ = 0.…

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 3. Scientific Definitions | Term | Scientific meaning | Example | |---|---|---| | **Product rule** | (fg)′ = f′g + fg′ | sin x·cos x | | **Chain rule** | (f∘g)′ = f′(g)·g′ | ln(sin x) | | **Parametric dy/dx** | (dy/dt)/(dx/dt) | ellipse tangents | | **Logarithmic diff** | ln y first, then solve | xˣ |  ·  ## 4. Detailed Explanation ### 4.1 Why the chain rule is the master rule - Product and quotient rules are special cases of treating expressions as composites; every "hard" derivative is a chain rule in disguise. Master dy/du · du/dx and the table becomes universal.…  ·  ## 5. Comparison Tables **Rule selector** | Situation | Rule | |---|---| | product of functions | (fg)′ = f′g + fg′ | | quotient | (f′g − fg′)/g² | | composite | f′(g)·g′ | | x = x(t), y = y(t) | (dy/dt)/(dx/dt) | | equation in x, y | implicit + solve | | u^v both variable | logarithmic diff |

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **NEB-style (5m): If y = A cos(mx) + B sin(mx), show that d²y/dx² + m²y = 0.** — **First derivative (linearity + chain):** y′ = A(−m sin mx) + B(m cos mx) = **−Am sin mx + Bm cos mx**. **Second derivative:** y′′ = −Am(m cos mx) + Bm(−m sin mx) = **−m²(A cos mx + B sin mx) = −m²y**. **Rearrange: y′′ + m²y = 0** ∎.…  ·  **NEB-style (6m): If y = (sin x)^{cos x}, show that dy/dx = y(cos x·cot x − sin x·log_e(sin x)), and find dy/dx at x = π/4.** — **Logarithmic differentiation:** ln y = cos x·ln(sin x).…  ·  Differentiate sin x·cos x by the product rule.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Limit to remember: derivative f'(x) = lim_{h→0} [f(x+h) − f(x)]/h = tangent slope; rules: sum, product, quotient, chain.  ·  ## 6. Common Confusions **Chain rule amnesia:** ln(sin x) is cot x only because the inner derivative cos x survives — dropping u′ is the classic error.  ·  **Parametric second derivative:** divide by dx/dt again after differentiating dy/dx in t — not the ratio of second t-derivatives.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **x^x is not x·x^{x−1}:** the power rule needs constant exponent; xˣ demands logarithmic differentiation.  ·  ## 7. Exam Application **NEB 2023 (verified PYQ): Find the derivative of y = sin x · cos x using the product rule. (3m)** — **Product rule:** y′ = (sin x)′·cos x + sin x·(cos x)′ = cos x·cos x + sin x·(−sin x) = cos²x − sin²x = **cos 2x**. (Cross-check: y = ½ sin 2x ⟹ y′ = ½·2cos 2x = cos 2x ✓.)  ·  **NEB 2022 (verified PYQ): Differentiate (i) y = xˣ, (ii) y = sin²x·eˣ, (iii) y = (1+x)^{1/x}. (3m)** — **(i) Logarithmic:** ln y = x ln x ⟹ y′/y = ln x + 1 ⟹ **y′ = xˣ(ln x + 1)**. **(ii) Product + chain:** y′ = (2 sin x cos x)·eˣ + sin²x·eˣ = **eˣ(sin 2x + sin²x)**.…
